new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls regularly and strongly on the final syllable of the word; Segai words are mostly monosyllabic (CCV(C), after deletion of penultimate vowels) or sesquisyllabic with an unstressed schwa presyllable, so the single full-vowel final syllable carries the stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None; stress described as regular/across-the-board word-final. Kelai and Gaai retain a few penultimate vowels (irregularly or to avoid disallowed clusters) but no stress exception is stated for them.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement made for the Segai-Modang subgroup as a whole, with Gaai (Long Laai, Segah river) and Punan Kelai (Long Lamjan, Kelai river) as the Segai members in Smith's own 2015-16 field data (c. 1,000-item vocabularies plus sentence lists); no phrase-level or acoustic detail.
new_statements.identity_note: Smith's statement is made for the Segai-Modang subgroup and instantiated by his own field data on Gaai (Mengga'ai) of Long Laai on the upper Segah river and Punan Kelai of Long Lamjan (Long Palai) on the Kelai river, Berau Regency; Smith 2017:77 assigns 'Gaai, Punan Kelai, and all similar languages of the Berau area along the Segah and Kelai rivers' to the Segai group, i.e. Glottolog sega1243 / ISO sge (Wikipedia lists Kelai and Segah as its dialects). Smith 2019 adds Wahau as a third Segai variety. The sister Modang varieties (Long Gelat, Woq Helaq/Kelinjau, Mei Lan) fall under moda1244, covered by the same statement.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Abstract (proof p.1 = OL p.353): 'Segai-Modang languages are stress-final and have innovated sesqui- and monosyllabic canonical word forms'. Sec. 3 (proof p.6): word shape 'associated with across-the-board stress shift to the final syllable'. Sec. 7 Conclusion (proof p.26, ~OL p.378): 'regular word-final stress of the modern languages'. Data primary for Wahau, Gaai, Kelai (= Segai), Mei Lan, Woq Helaq, Long Gelat (= Modang).
